newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares edge up, sideways drift seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares edge up, sideways drift seen.

text.p: Polish shares edged up in stable trade on Tuesday and analysts expected them to stay flat as the lack of new signals and psychological resistance seen at recent highs made investors uncertain about the future.
The main market's WIG index rose 9.6 points, or 0.1 percent, to 14,753.6 and total turnover was stable at 123.5 million zlotys ($44.1 million) as 35 issues rose, 25 fell and 18 were flat.

They said the market this week could gain the 0.5 percent necessary to challenge the main index's September 18, 30-month high of 14,832.7 points, but that higher turnovers were needed to signal that a new record would provide strong support.

"Investors are uncertain if the market is strong enough to pierce recent highs or whether it would bounce off that resistance, so they may adopt a wait-and-see approch," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Analysts said the market was likely to get a push when inflation data for September and companies' September earnings reports, both due in mid-October, are released.
They said if the reports proved good they could push the market to new highs and start a new growth trend which could place the market at 15,200 or 15,750 points of WIG.
But some analysts feared a profit-taking correction after the 90-percent growth since December 1995 and said the market could fall to 12,500 points before year-end.
Continuous trade turnover was at two million zlotys with biggest mover steel trader Stalexport falling 3.8 percent.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell three percent in a 21.5-million- zloty ($7.7 million) turnover in the bourse's regular session and fell 3.1 percent in 16.5-million-zloty ($5.9 million) continuous trade.
